title: #15 #14: an issuer whose ticket is no longer its own stops without writing anything
objective: An issuer whose ticket is no longer running under the stamp it wrote at its claim writes nothing more to the pool, moves no branch, stops its agents and exits 2.
outline: ticket_issuer.py: claim() keeps the stamp it writes (self.run_stamp). Issuer.save(): inside change(tx), after the claim, raise a new exception (e.g. NotOwned) before mutate when tx.ticket(id) is not state running with run == self.run_stamp; nothing is written (the exception leaves pool.update before any tx.write). integrate(): an ownership check (snapshot read) before g.merge(self.target) and before self.repo.move_ref. _go(): NotOwned -> stop_agents(), print one line 'ticket_issuer: #N is no longer this issuer's ticket (state <s>); stopped without writing', return 2. The Stuck and Interrupted handlers end with a save (stuck(), release()): a NotOwned raised there must give the same line and rc 2, not _safe's 'could not record the outcome' (stuck() writes its page only after its save, so no page follows). Optionally check ownership before apply_unapplied at round start. Update the docstring's exit line (2 also: the ticket is no longer this issuer's) and the README's Contracts exit-code line if it lists issuer codes.

(p2) A ticket set to ready under a running issuer (what _release_orphan writes) was merged by that issuer anyway: int/g1 moved, ready became merged, rc 0. Not measured: which part of T's macOS stamp the controller judged dead (boot id = the text of `sysctl -n kern.boottime`, or the host name); the lock makes it irrelevant, since the kernel frees a flock only when its holder dies. (p3) The run stamp replaced by another one while the issuer's worker ran: the issuer merged anyway (state merged, int/g1 moved, rc 0). With the lock ticket of this hand-in no second issuer starts; this ticket covers every other way a ticket can leave its issuer (an older controller, a hand edit, an issuer started before the lock existed) so that the stale one cannot merge it, turn a merged or landed ticket into stuck or remove nothing it does not own. Never write os.kill, killpg, pkill or the text 'kill -' in any added line (code, tests, comments, strings): board/config.json hard_block matches them and stops the ticket before merge. Use osx.alive, osx.kill_tree, Popen.terminate or Popen.send_signal instead. Group new-g1: same files and one regression as the other #14/#15 tickets.
acceptance: When the ticket is set to state ready with run null (what Controller._release_orphan writes) while its issuer's worker runs, the issuer exits 2 once the worker's run returns; its stderr has exactly one non-empty line, containing '#1 is no longer this issuer's ticket'; afterwards the ticket's state, run, round, feedback, cost and cases are what that write left, its history ends with that write's event, int/g1 points where it pointed when the issuer started, and the inbox holds no page whose ref is '1'.

When the ticket's run is replaced by another stamp (state stays running) while its issuer's worker runs, the same holds: exit 2, the one line, the ticket as that write left it (run equal to the other stamp, no event after it), int/g1 unchanged, no page about #1.

Every write the issuer makes to its ticket after the claim (round start, cases ready, cases thrown out, feedback, the quota marks, merged, stuck, the release after a signal) checks inside the same pool update that the ticket is running with the issuer's own claim stamp, and writes nothing when it is not; integrate() re-reads the ticket before it merges the target into the ticket branch and before it moves the target, and does neither when the ticket is not its own.

## Issue #15: a restarted controller starts a second issuer for a running ticket
T (A at b5564f9, macOS): after a controller restart done as #11's answer recommends (SIGTERM to `ticket_controller.py --forever` only, children left running), the old issuer of #320 (pid 84547, started by the previous controller, ppid 1 after the restart, running r3-worker through a wrapper `alternate.sh -> agy.sh`) was not adopted: the new controller started a second `ticket_issuer.py --id 320` (pid 66766), which ran an r2-worker in the same worktree `t320` on `t/320`. The r2 worker saw the other run and handed in `blocked`; #320 went stuck. The orphan then began merging main into t/320 (20:15:17 local). It ignored SIGTERM (agy.sh waits for agy) and had to be SIGKILLed.
What the main session read in the code (inference, not measured):
- The controller adopts a live issuer by the ticket's `run` stamp (ticket_controller.py finish_jobs, osx.stamp_dead). A second issuer can only start after the ticket is back to ready: `_release_orphan` (stamp judged dead) or the issuer's own `release()` on a signal (ticket_issuer.py _go, Interrupted), which sets ready and round-1. The new issuer running r2 while the old one ran r3 fits the second: the old issuer got a signal, released the ticket (r3 -> round 2), and then did not exit - its interrupted_costs/stop_agents path may block on a wrapper that ignores SIGTERM, or the process went on to the merge step.
- Find out which, by reproducing with the loop harness (a fake agent command that ignores SIGTERM; stop the controller as T did; also signal the issuer). Write the measured cause in the ticket.
Wanted:
- A ticket never has two issuers at once: the issuer holds a per-ticket lock (flock on a file under the worktrees root, like gitx's worktree lock) for its whole life; a second issuer for the same id refuses at once (exit 2, one line) and touches nothing.
- An issuer that has released its ticket (interrupted) does no further work on it: no merge, no push, no pool write other than the release; it stops its agents' process trees (kill_tree, escalating to SIGKILL after a short grace when a wrapper ignores SIGTERM) and exits.
- A restarted controller adopts a live issuer (stamp alive) and does not dispatch the ticket again while that issuer (or its lock) lives.

## Issue #14: a ticket's worktree disappears during a chain fall-through after quota
T: three cases on 2026-11-24 (#369 reviewer, #351 worker, #354 reviewer): the first command of the role's chain (agy.sh) said "usage limit reached"; about 3 minutes later the next command (claude) could not start: `no command for reviewer could start (cannot start claude: not found ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../tabby_pool_wt/devloop/t369'))`. By then `t369` and `t369-cases` were gone and not in `git worktree list`. The ticket went stuck.
Inference (main session, not measured): the cases were the same afternoon as #15; a second issuer for the same ticket that ends (stuck) runs `Issuer.cleanup()` and removes the worktrees the first issuer still uses. Check this first; if it is not the cause, find what removed the worktree (grep every remove_worktree / prune / rmtree caller).
